summary: The note describes the 1972 Federation Cup, the tenth edition of the premier women's tennis competition between national teams. Thirty-one nations took part in the event, held at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, South Africa, from 20 to 25 March. South Africa beat Great Britain in the final, the first final without the United States or Australia, and became the first team outside those two nations to win the cup.
one_line: The 1972 Federation Cup, a women's tennis team event held at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, was won by South Africa over Great Britain.
key_facts: The 1972 Federation Cup was the tenth edition of the Federation Cup.
The Federation Cup is described as the most important competition between national teams in women's tennis.
31 nations participated in the 1972 Federation Cup.
The 1972 Federation Cup was held at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, South Africa.
The 1972 Federation Cup was held from 20 to 25 March.
South Africa defeated Great Britain in the 1972 Federation Cup final.
The 1972 final was the first Federation Cup final not featuring the United States or Australia.
South Africa won its first Federation Cup title in 1972.
South Africa became the first team other than the United States or Australia to win the Fed Cup.
